You'd be surprised how often I've seen confusion around basic table etiquette. I'm not an expert at this so if anyone that attended cotillion feel free to correct me or add. If you're confronted with multiple utensils at the table you're generally going to use the outside utensils first. For example, if there are two forks and a salad is going to be served use the outer most fork for the salad. If you skip the salad, skip the fork. There is also a very easy way to cheat this, simply wait until everyone starts eating and use the utensils they use. Which brings me to another point, wait until everyone has their food before you start eating. If someone else tells you to begin, then go for it.

Now let's back up a bit to bread. Yes, bread. It is a very rare sight to see people eat bread properly at dinner. Many people will rip it in half and butter the entire thing then eat it like a sandwich. While efficient, this isn't the correct way to do this. The proper way to eat bread at dinner is to break a bite sized piece off using both hands, butter the piece, eat it, then repeat.

For the end of the meal, your utensils should be placed on the plate. I was taught that they should be placed at the top quarter of the plate with the handles pointing to the right, however it seems that the more conventional/proper method is to place them in the middle of the plate with the handles facing towards you. Also, after your meal do not keep your utensils. If you're going to have desert they'll bring new ones.
